title: National Mining Association: US mining trade association landing page
answer: This is the landing page of the National Mining Association, the US mining industry's national trade association. It says NMA is the only national trade organization serving as the voice of US mining before Congress, federal agencies, the judiciary and the media. Its most useful point for policy watchers is that it advocates for public policies on secure supply chains, affordable energy, American sourced materials, and environmental, safety and labor standards. It does not discuss artificial intelligence or give regulatory detail.

sections.body: The National Mining Association publishes this page. It is a trade association landing page, not a report or dataset. It states that NMA is the official voice of US mining and the only national trade organization representing the industry before Congress, federal agencies, the judiciary and the media. Its scope is the US mining industry and the hundreds of thousands of American workers it employs. No publication date is given.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents the National Mining Association as the official voice of US mining. It says NMA is the only national trade organization that serves as the voice of the US mining industry and the hundreds of thousands of American workers it employs before Congress, the federal agencies, the judiciary and the media. Its stated purpose is to advocate for public policies that help America fully and responsibly utilize its vast natural resources. It says NMA works to ensure America has secure and reliable supply chains, abundant and affordable energy, and American sourced materials necessary for US manufacturing and economic security. It adds that these are delivered under world leading environmental, safety and labor standards. The page also says NMA will help readers navigate the complex political, regulatory and industry scene by engaging in and influencing the public process on the most significant and timely issues that impact mining today. Finally, it states that mining is the foundation of the economy and national security, providing materials, manufacturing inputs and power for nearly every industry and product, and that it keeps the lights on and supply chains secure for families and businesses across the US.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives one quantity: the US mining industry employs hundreds of thousands of American workers. It also makes these claims: NMA is the official voice of US mining, it is the only national trade organization serving that role, it advocates before Congress, federal agencies, the judiciary and the media, and it works for secure supply chains, affordable energy, American sourced materials, and environmental, safety and labor standards. No other numbers, dates or definitions are given.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in mining would use this page to identify the US policy layer for the sector. It names the National Mining Association as the industry's national trade organization and says it engages in the public process on significant mining issues before Congress, federal agencies, the judiciary and the media. That is relevant background for anyone tracking how mining regulation and public policy develop, but the page does not discuss AI, automation or technology adoption, so it cannot support claims about AI use in mining.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Mining

sections.body: This is a short advocacy landing page. It gives no date, no regulatory detail, no data on technology adoption and no mention of artificial intelligence. It is promotional in tone and presents the association's own view of its role. It does not cover specific mines, companies, operations or policy positions beyond broad goals. A reader should treat it as a starting point for the NMA's stated mission, not as a detailed or independent source.
